report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/eval/mint.py chunk 3 of 3, lines 561-...; enumerated all docstring/comment claims and verified against visible code; all verdicts KEPT or UNCHECKABLE; no BROKEN claims.
risks: mint_from_commit | medium | 'never raises' claim is uncheckable because _git and _show can raise and are not wrapped; to settle, inspect _git/_show implementations for exception handling.

mint_from_commit | medium | 'Returns [] for unresolvable ref, no in-scope file, or single in-scope file' is only partially verifiable; the single-file case is delegated to _mint_from_diffs, which is outside this chunk; to settle, inspect _mint_from_diffs for that condition.
mint_task_from_landed_edit | medium | 'Returns None if every write is symbol-identical to HEAD' is delegated to _mint_from_diffs; to settle, inspect _mint_from_diffs for the no-diff condition.
mint_from_commit | medium | '...or one where only a single in-scope file has a diffed symbol' is delegated to _mint_from_diffs; to settle, inspect _mint_from_diffs for the single-file condition.
save_minted_tasks | low | Writes with open(...,'w') without fsync or atomic replace; a crash mid-write could corrupt the store; to settle, inspect surrounding persistence robustness requirements.

load_minted_tasks | low | Parses JSON with no schema validation; malformed store would raise, contradicting 'read the persisted mint store' robustness; to settle, inspect expected store format and error handling.
confirm_minted_task | low | Loads tasks, mutates, saves; concurrent writers could lose updates; to settle, inspect concurrency model (single-process assumption).

handoff.purpose: Review minting, persistence, and confirmation functions and their documented guarantees.

symbols.name: _log_mint_diagnostics
symbols.note: Logs skipped files and reason at INFO; no side effects beyond logging.

symbols.name: mint_task_from_landed_edit
symbols.note: Reads git HEAD and worktree; returns task dict or None; no writes.

symbols.name: mint_from_commit
symbols.note: Reads git commit; returns list of task dicts; no writes.

symbols.name: confirm_task
symbols.note: Mutates task dict in place; promotes tier to primary at threshold.

symbols.name: load_minted_tasks
symbols.note: Reads JSON store; returns sorted list; returns [] if missing.

symbols.name: save_minted_tasks
symbols.note: Writes JSON store with deterministic formatting; returns path.

symbols.name: add_minted_task
symbols.note: Loads store, upserts by id, saves; returns path.

symbols.name: confirm_minted_task
symbols.note: Loads store, confirms one task by id, saves; returns updated task or None.

claims.text: The 'reported, never silent' channel for information that doesn't fit the two public mint_* entry points' pre-existing ``dict | None`` / ``list[dict]`` return shape
claims.why: Function logs the diagnostics; the claim describes its role, which matches the code's logging behavior.

claims.text: A task that DID mint carries its own ``skipped_out_of_scope``/``must_include_dropped`` fields; this is what surfaces the same information -- and the no-task-minted ``reason`` -- for the cases where there is no task dict to carry it.
claims.why: Function logs skipped_out_of_scope and reason from diagnostics dict; the corresponding fields are set in the task dict earlier (visible in the first lines of the chunk).

claims.text: ``report['wrote']`` IS ``disk_changed`` from offload.py:194-197 -- the files that ACTUALLY changed on disk, found by diffing a before/after content-hash snapshot taken around the run.
claims.why: The claim references offload.py:194-197 and details of offload's behavior; that file is not in this chunk, so the equivalence cannot be verified here.

claims.text: The model's self-reported ``files_changed`` is deliberately not read
claims.why: The function only reads report.get('wrote') and never accesses files_changed.

claims.text: The edit is assumed uncommitted (offload writes straight into the working tree and never commits): 'before' is read from git HEAD, 'after' from the file currently on disk.
claims.why: Code uses _show(repo_root, 'HEAD', rel) for before and _read_worktree(repo_root, rel) for after.

claims.text: A file the run created has no HEAD blob (before = None); a file it deleted has nothing left on disk (after = None).
claims.why: The behavior of _show and _read_worktree is not visible in this chunk; the claim depends on those functions returning None for absent blobs/files.

claims.text: Returns ``None`` if there is nothing to mint: no writes reported, every write's content is symbol-identical to HEAD (e.g. a formatting-only touch this diff granularity can't see through), no written file is in the project's index scope, or only one in-scope file has a diffed symbol (no cross-file label exists -- see the module docstring's CROSS-FILE ONLY rule).
claims.why: The no-writes case is verifiable (returns None if disk_changed empty), but the symbol-identical, out-of-scope, and single-file cases are delegated to _mint_from_diffs, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Same idea as ``mint_task_from_landed_edit``, but against history that already exists -- this is what lets minting be exercised deterministically in tests without a live offload run (a temp git fixture IS real git history; ``git show`` gives exact before/after text with no mocking).
claims.why: The function uses git commands (_git, _show) against a real commit; the claim about test determinism is consistent with the code's use of real git history.

claims.text: Currently mints a single aggregate task per commit (via the same ``_mint_from_diffs`` used for landed edits); returns a list so a future split (e.g. one task per hunk, for very large commits) is additive rather than a signature change.
claims.why: The function calls _mint_from_diffs once and returns [task] if task else [].

claims.text: Returns ``[]`` for an unresolvable ref, a commit that touches no in-scope file, or one where only a single in-scope file has a diffed symbol (no cross-file label exists) -- never raises.
claims.why: Unresolvable ref is handled (returns [] if _resolve_sha returns None), and _git failure is handled (returns [] if name_status is None), but the no-in-scope-file and single-file cases are delegated to _mint_from_diffs, which is not in this chunk. The 'never raises' claim is uncheckable because _git and _show could raise and are not wrapped.

claims.text: --root: a commit with no parent (the very first commit of history) is diffed against the empty tree instead of silently producing no rows.
claims.why: The code passes --root to git diff-tree, and parent is None for root commits, so before is None for all files.

claims.text: Promotes ``task['tier']`` from ``'quarantine'`` to ``'primary'`` once ``confirmations`` reaches ``MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD``.
claims.why: The code increments confirmations and sets tier to 'primary' when confirmations >= MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD.

claims.text: A no-op on a task that is not currently quarantined: a primary task doesn't need more confirming, and 'confirming' a hand_reachable task is meaningless -- it was never gated in the first place.
claims.why: The function returns early if task.get('tier') != 'quarantine', leaving the dict unchanged.

claims.text: Returns the same (mutated) dict for convenient chaining; callers that need the pre-mutation task should copy it first.
claims.why: The function returns the same dict object after mutation.

claims.text: Read the persisted mint store, or ``[]`` if it does not exist yet.
claims.why: The function returns [] if os.path.exists(p) is False.

claims.text: This is the ONLY load path by which a minted task can reach ``daedalus.eval.harness.all_tasks()`` and therefore any go/no-go number -- without it, ``mint_task_from_landed_edit``/``mint_from_commit`` produced dicts that lived only as long as the caller's local variable.
claims.why: The claim concerns harness.all_tasks() and the broader system; that module is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Sorted by id for deterministic iteration (PYTHONHASHSEED-independent), matching the rest of this repo's output-determinism rule.
claims.why: The function returns sorted(data.get('tasks', []), key=lambda t: t['id']).

claims.text: Overwrite the mint store with exactly ``tasks``. Deterministic formatting (sorted keys, sorted by id) so the diff is meaningful in review -- same contract as ``harness.write_baseline``.
claims.why: The function sorts tasks by id and writes with json.dump(sort_keys=True, indent=2) and a trailing newline.

claims.text: Returns the path written.
claims.why: The function returns p.

claims.text: Persist ``task`` into the mint store, keyed by id. Idempotent: minting the same diff twice (same target + same must_include, via the content hash in ``_mint_from_diffs``) yields the same id and overwrites in place rather than duplicating -- re-running a mint (e.g. after a rebase that reproduces an identical patch) must not inflate the quarantine count.
claims.why: The function builds a dict keyed by id and overwrites by_id[task['id']] = task, then saves; duplicate ids are overwritten.

claims.text: Returns the path written.
claims.why: The function returns save_minted_tasks(...), which returns the path.

claims.text: Load the store, confirm ONE task by id (see ``confirm_task``), persist the mutation, and return the updated task -- or ``None`` if ``task_id`` is not in the store.
claims.why: The function loads tasks, loops to find matching id, calls confirm_task (mutating in place), saves, and returns the task; returns None if not found.

claims.text: The only durable way a quarantined mint accumulates confirmations and eventually promotes to primary; ``confirm_task`` alone only mutates an in-memory dict that would otherwise evaporate.
claims.why: The function persists the mutated tasks list; confirm_task alone does not save.

observations.what: mint_from_commit's 'never raises' claim is not fully verifiable from this chunk because _git and _show can raise and are not wrapped.
The single-in-scope-file and no-in-scope-file conditions are delegated to _mint_from_diffs, which is not in this chunk, so those parts of the return-value claims are uncheckable.
save_minted_tasks writes without fsync or atomic replace; a crash mid-write could corrupt the store, which may conflict with the determinism/review contract.
load_minted_tasks does not validate the JSON schema; a malformed store would raise, which may conflict with the 'read the persisted mint store' robustness implied by the docstring.
confirm_minted_task is not atomic against concurrent writers (load-modify-save); concurrent confirmations could lose updates.
